question: Can an unexecuted JOWA search branch modify the cache or observation history used for the factual branch or next real decision through storage aliasing?

contract_and_scope.required_invariant: Given the same real observation/action history, merely evaluating and discarding a hypothetical branch must not append its imagined tokens to the factual history or mutate another branch's cache through shared storage.
contract_and_scope.not_required: Search scores and the selected real action may legitimately depend on hypothetical branch forecasts. This ordinary planning effect is not history contamination.
contract_and_scope.permission_status: This is a source-level reachability screen. No separately deployed multi-tenant query service or attacker permission to mutate internal caches was established or added.
contract_and_scope.goal_bus_boundary: The native environment/game identifier selects Atari task context, including the dynamics/action vocabulary. It is not an independently writable preference-only Goal. Swapping it would not inherit a fixed-physics Goal-invariance contract.
contract_and_scope.deduplication: JOWA was not in the existing mechanism registry. Unlike the already tested TD-MPC warm-start and OPINE global-memory paths, this candidate specifically concerned native search-branch cache ownership; replacing the carrier alone would not establish novelty.

native_decision_path.path: For horizon greater than zero, native beam search expands predicted observation tokens and rewards, reads successor Q values, ranks nodes by discounted cumulative predicted reward plus terminal max Q, and returns the winning path's first action. Horizon zero selects the root Q maximum.

decisive_code_facts: Every native planning call creates a new WorldModelEnv and deep-copies its initial cache for the root node.
concate_kv and split_kv allocate new cache storage and copy valid prefixes; they do not expose shared branch prefix storage.
WorldModelEnv.obs_tokens initially may view the factual token buffer, but step rebinds it to a new torch.cat result rather than writing the imagined tokens into that buffer.
The persistent Agent token buffer is updated with encoded actual observations and the action passed to the real environment, not with discarded forecast tokens.

cpu_probe.method: Directly import upstream cache classes. Exercise deepcopy, concatenation, splitting, pruning, prefix writes and size changes with small CPU sentinel tensors. Compile the unchanged upstream step method with a synthetic parameter-free token producer and lightweight readout/decoder.
cpu_probe.positive_control: A deliberately aliased reference changes its owner, confirming the detector can observe a write. This artificial control is not a native defect.
cpu_probe.observed: Native copy operations preserve root and sibling valid prefixes and sizes. An explicit step cache advances from 2 to 5 tokens while the member root remains at 2; observation rebinding preserves the factual token buffer.
cpu_probe.limits: No checkpoint, learned prediction, Atari episode, full Agent/MCTS execution, two-successive-plan integration, concurrency or shared-model/RNG-state test. This excludes the inspected storage-aliasing path, not every possible JOWA dependency.

separate_mcts_correctness_issue.finding: MCTS passes deepcopy(parent.kv_cache) to step, but afterwards saves deepcopy(wm_env.keys_values_wm) into the child. The explicit cache is advanced while the environment member cache is not, so the child receives the stale initialization prefix.
separate_mcts_correctness_issue.confirmation_scope: Pinned call-site inspection plus execution of the original step method on synthetic tensors confirms the ownership mismatch; the complete MCTS algorithm and trained model were not executed.
separate_mcts_correctness_issue.reason_not_attack_success: No adversarial operation or trust-boundary violation has been demonstrated. A stale search prefix is different from an unexecuted branch overwriting factual history.

reopen_condition: A materially different, reachable state-writing path or new evidence contradicting the observed isolation, with an explicit contract and proposed decisive native utility test. A generic MCTS correctness fix, new carrier name or mere forecast difference is not sufficient.
review: Two independent source reviewers agreed with the bounded candidate No-Go. One separately identified the remaining full-plan/RNG/model-state integration limits. No claim of universal system safety is made.
